messages:
Alex (eng-platform): Quick sync — we need a final decision on quota band definitions and how burst should behave across free / pro / enterprise. Thinking about both per-org and per-key behavior.
Maria (product): TL;DR: free gets very limited steady rate with tiny burst; pro gets higher steady + controlled burst; enterprise gets large steady + configurable burst windows. Need the exact numbers though.
Sam (finance): We need the mapping to be revenue-friendly but predictable. If burst for free is too generous we're bleeding credits. Pro should get a meaningful uplift vs free, enterprise should have SLA-backed headroom.
Jordan (devex): UX note — console should show both current usage and the remaining burst budget clearly. Don’t surface too many knobs though.
Alex (eng-platform): Proposal v1 (very rough):
```
free: steady=60 req/min, burst=300 req for 30s window (cooldown 15m)
pro: steady=600 req/min, burst=3k req for 60s window (cooldown 5m)
enterprise: steady=10k req/min, burst=50k req for 120s window (configurable)
```
Alex (eng-platform): Behavior detail: burst is a short-lived overflow lane that consumes a burst budget. Once budget is depleted, requests fall back to steady limit. Burst budget replenishes linearly over cooldown.
Maria (product): I like the idea but can we make free burst even smaller? 300 for 30s might be fine but only once per hour? Maybe tie to daily budget instead of cooldown.
Sam (finance): Agree with Maria — free should be gated: small per-day burst allowance (e.g., 2k/day) so we don't see bots spike and exhaust credits. Pro/external metrics show big spikes cost us.
Jordan (devex): Implementation complexity note: per-key burst + per-org pooling interact weirdly. If org-level pooling is on, keys within org should share a single burst budget; otherwise keys get independent budgets. Which behavior do we want?
Alex (eng-platform): Default: org-pooling ON for pro+enterprise, OFF for free. That way pro teams benefit from shared headroom. We'll add a console toggle for enterprise.
Maria (product): UX: in billing UI show "Burst usage this billing cycle" and an example of how a burst consumed tokens map to cost. Also show predicted next-burst availability.
Sam (finance): Pricing mapping: map free->Free plan, pro->Pro monthly, enterprise->Enterprise contract. Add a small premium for burst-heavy usage on Pro (e.g., add-on: "burst-overage" priced per 10k tokens).
Jordan (devex): Routing policy: when steady/full, requests should route to cheaper capacity (spot/dedicated fallback) but burst traffic prefers low-latency nodes. Need RFC for routing preference.
Alex (eng-platform): Action items: 1) Eng to prototype burst budget algorithm & per-org pooling (owner: Alex) 2) Product to finalize numbers for free/pro/enterprise + console copy (owner: Maria) 3) Finance to propose burst-overage pricing (owner: Sam) 4) Devex to draft console mockups for burst visibility (owner: Jordan).
Maria (product): I'll ping legal once we finalize enterprise config (configurable burst windows might need clause).
QuotaBot: Reminder: quota rule change alert will be staged to canary orgs tomorrow at 10:00 UTC.
Sam (finance): :thumbsup: If we can get pro numbers by EOD Wednesday we can include in next pricing announcement.
Jordan (devex): I'll mock a simplified chart for the console — pro shows pooled budget line, free shows per-key tiny bars.
Alex (eng-platform): Thanks all. We'll reconvene after eng prototype for real numbers. If anyone wants to change defaults, comment here.
Maria (product): One last ask — add a 1-click "request temporary burst increase" flow for enterprise in the console (ticket + audit).
Alex (eng-platform): noted. Closing thread after prototypes land.
